question: True or false: a patch of octopus skin, cut away from the body, still reacts to light?
answer: True. In excised skin of the California two-spot octopus, light made the pigment sacs called chromatophores expand, fastest under blue light. The skin makes opsin, the light-detecting protein of eyes, in its own sensory cells. With no eye and no brain attached, a cut patch of skin still flushed dark under a lamp.
move: Before assuming a signal comes from the centre, test the edge alone.
trap: Colour change seems to need the eyes and brain to direct it.
reference: Ramirez & Oakley, Eye-independent, light-activated chromatophore expansion (LACE) and expression of phototransduction genes in the skin of Octopus bimaculoides, Journal of Experimental Biology, 2015
